headline: Poliomyelitis in Tennessee
source: American Journal of Public Health (via PubMed Central)
blurb: A paper on polio in Tennessee by W. C. Williams, read at a public health meeting in St. Louis on November 19, 1935, was published in the American Journal of Public Health in February 1936.

headline: A compulsory school immunization program in Tennessee.
blurb: In April 1978, Tennessee lawmakers extended the state's 1967 school vaccination law to all students in kindergarten through grade 12 at state-supported schools and kept the medical and religious exemptions.

headline: Epidemiologic Notes and Reports Rubella Outbreak among Foreign- Exchange Students -- Tennessee
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: On August 3, 1981, the University of Tennessee at Martin reported that seven Japanese exchange students had been hospitalized with suspected rubella, and 188 visiting students and faculty were vaccinated the next day.

headline: Measles Outbreak of Unknown Source — Shelby County, Tennessee, April–May 2016
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Seven measles cases were confirmed in Shelby County, Tennessee, in April and May 2016, and six of the seven patients were unvaccinated.

headline: TDH Continues Response to Hepatitis A Outbreak
source: Tennessee Department of Health (archived by the Internet Archive)
blurb: The Tennessee Department of Health said a hepatitis A outbreak had reached more than 400 cases and one death, with Nashville and Chattanooga most heavily affected.

headline: TDH Confirms First Tennessee Measles Case for 2019
source: Tennessee Department of Health (archived by the Internet Archive)
blurb: The Tennessee Department of Health confirmed the state's first measles case of 2019 in a resident of East Tennessee.
